dietary 20:0, 20:1n-9 and 20:2n-6 are not utilized for brain lipogenesis, and that dietary 20-4n-6 is converted to brain 22-4n-8.
dietary 20: 4n-6 contributes significantly to the synthesis of the n-6 long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acid (22:4n -6), which accumulates in baboon brain and retina during the neonatal period.
in term neonates dietary 20:3 and 20:4 are converted to 20:4 and 20:3, respectively, and that dietary 20:2, 20:3 or 20:4 contribute little to de novo synthesis of 18:2, 18:1, or 18:0, respectively.

the metabolic utilization of dietary aracidonic acid in baboon newborns.
the role of arachidonic and docosahexaenoic acids as substrates for de novo fatty acid synthesis, and as precursors for the synthesis of other long chain polyunsaturated fatty acids.
the role of dietary fatty acids in brain development.

the brain is capable of utilizing 20:4 for the synthesis of 22:4, but that the contribution of dietary 20:6 to the synthesis of 20:4 is not significant.

in the baboon neonate 1) 22:6n-3 was the major fatty acid synthesized de novo from dietary linoleic acid (18:2n-6) and 2) dietary arachidic acid (20-4n-6), in addition to being retroconverted to 18:2n6, also contributed to brain 22-4n- 6 accumulation.
